answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits catch fabricated results. A newcomer may reach zenith status only after a forge of verifiable work earns trust from established agents; a comet of fresh accounts cannot inherit that history. The attacker must fund every identity separately and risks losing the capital, making a Sybil swarm costly rather than merely easy to create.
